issues.title: Main-screen warnings: tell players the ladder can fork BEFORE they play (draft copy inside)
issues.body:
Requested by Pip, 2026-07-30: *"Maybe we can have a more explicit set of warnings posted
on the main page of the UI of the game."* Context is the L2 -> L3 mid-month fork and his
own note that **"ladder integrity will probably break this week, that's fine and
expected"** — the point being that players should learn that from the game, not from
finding their score gone.

Drafted from the website side because the same statement has to appear on
`/leaderboard/`, and the two should not say different things. **The game's wording is
the authority; the website will follow whatever lands here.** Reword freely.

## The principle worth keeping, whatever the wording

A player who loses a score should have been told it could happen **before** they played,
not consoled afterwards. The warning is cheap; the trust is not. Three things follow:

1. **State the risk, not a reassurance.** "May be reset" is honest. "Your scores are
   safe" is a promise the alpha cannot keep.
2. **Never claim a score is permanent.** Scores are keyed to a ladder epoch and epochs
   fork. That is by design, and it should read as design, not as an accident.
3. **Say it where the decision is made** — before the run, on the screen a player looks
   at when choosing to play, not buried in a settings page or a changelog.

## Suggested copy

### A. Persistent line on the main/welcome screen

Short enough to live permanently without becoming wallpaper:

> **ALPHA — scores and rules change between releases.**
> Leaderboards are tied to a rules version. When the rules change, a new board opens and
> earlier scores stay on the old one.

### B. Expanded panel (behind an "i" / "What does that mean?" affordance)

> **P(Doom)1 is in alpha, and the rules are still moving.**
>
> Each leaderboard is tied to a **ladder epoch** — a snapshot of the game's rules. When a
> release changes how the game plays, a new epoch opens and a fresh board starts.
>
> **Your earlier scores are not deleted, and they are not carried forward either.** They
> stay on the board for the rules they were set under. A score from before a rules change
> cannot be fairly compared to one set after it, so we do not merge them.
>
> This will happen again. It is how the game stays honest about what a score means,
> rather than maintaining one ever-growing table that quietly mixes incompatible runs.
>
> Right now: **epoch L3**, opened 2026-07-31.

### C. One-time notice when the epoch changes under a returning player

Fires when the local build's ladder epoch differs from the one last seen:

> **New rules, new board.**
> The rules changed since you last played, so a new leaderboard has opened. Your previous
> scores are still recorded under the old rules — they are just not on this board.

## Two specifics that make this concrete this week

- The L3 fork removed the action-point pool entirely in favour of an attention economy,
  added office lease + lock-in, four-way founder hours, six previously-inert upgrades and
  a quirk rebalance. That is a big enough change that a player who does not know the
  board reset will assume a bug.
- **A small number of testers have genuinely stranded scores from before the fork.** Pip
  is contacting them personally, which is the right call — but the warning above is what
  stops the same conversation being needed next epoch.

## Where the epoch string should come from

`GameConfig.get_board_version()` / `ladder_version.txt`, rendered — **not typed into the
scene**. A hardcoded "L3" in a `.tscn` becomes a lie at the next fork, and this is a
warning whose whole job is to be true. Same class as pdoom1#1011 (derive keybind labels
rather than typing them) and the F8/N bug that came from typing a key into three files.

## Website side

Whatever lands here, `/leaderboard/` will carry a matching statement so a player who
never opens the game's welcome screen still sees it. Tracked at pdoom1-website#201.
Please comment here with the final wording, or just ship it and I will follow the scene
text.

issues.title: design(tempo): actions resolve instantly, so the early game has no rhythm -- time, sequencing, and the queue's promise
issues.body:
From Pip's recorded playtest of the re-cut 0.13.2 artifact, 2026-07-30 16:36. Transcript in `art_generated/audiodump/2026-07-30_16-36-55.transcript.md`.

Three observations that look separate and are one problem.

## 1. Nothing takes time

**[1:33]** *"we don't have any of the other actions taking time yet, I think, which is kind of throwing off some of the sequences. So like all the fundraising -- if I go and look at the plan, all of the fundraising happens on July the 4th, whereas what we need to do is have them take some time and then return a result later."*

Twenty actions were queued in about fifteen seconds and every one resolved on the same in-game date. There is no lead time, no in-flight period, and therefore no reason to sequence anything.

**This is upstream of a bug already fixed.** The action queue overflowed off-screen (#1039) partly *because* nothing leaves the queue -- instant resolution means the queue is a list of everything you have ever clicked this turn rather than a set of things currently happening. Widening the container treats the symptom.

It also undercuts the game's own deepest stated rule -- *"tragedy requires lead time"* -- which cannot be felt by the player if nothing the player does has any.

## 2. The early game does not teach the loop

**[4:33]** *"a little bit of a workshopping on making what actions players can and should be taking easier and more obvious by unlocking them more sequentially during the early game. We can give people options... but we encourage people to take maybe one of each of the higher network, fundraise, and other sets of actions so that people get used to sending things off, and we need to combine that with the things taking time so people are used to having stuff coming back."*

The ask is a **send-and-return rhythm**: dispatch something, wait, get a result. That rhythm cannot be taught while everything resolves instantly, which is why this and (1) are the same issue.

## 3. The queue should promise a completion time

**[5:02]** *"we probably want something like the action queuing system to have implied when are these things going to be done by us, but we need to think about that carefully."*

Once actions take time, the queue stops being a list and becomes a **schedule**. It should say when each thing lands. Pip flags this as wanting care, and it does -- it is the difference between a queue and a calendar, and it changes what the Plan screen is for.

## Why one issue

(2) is unteachable without (1). (3) is meaningless without (1) and is the natural UI consequence of it. Designing them separately produces a timing system with no onboarding and a queue that does not reflect it.

## Constraints already known

- **This forks the ladder.** Action durations change what happens on a fixed seed, so any implementation is an epoch bump (`RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md`). Not a patch.
- **Not this league.** Pip: *"it's a UI thing, so it doesn't need to change the ladder"* -- that was about the layout half (#1043). The timing half absolutely does change the ladder, and the distinction is worth keeping crisp.
- ADR-0011 effort economy and the founder-hours split are the substrate this lands on; ADR-0009's no-banking rule constrains what "in flight across a month boundary" can mean.

## Related

- #1043 -- the Plan-screen layout brief from the same afternoon; the dead middle is a candidate home for a schedule view
- #1041 -- morning playtest findings, incl. hiring actions not creating queue cards, which is the same queue-is-not-a-schedule confusion
- #1039 -- the overflow fix that treated the symptom
- #822 -- overbook TEETH, adjacent forcing-function work

issues.title: ui(layout): the Plan screen wastes its middle and scatters its text -- legibility-first layout brief
issues.body:
Captured via the **F6 flight recorder** during a 2026-07-30 16:44 session, at turn 1 with a fresh state (doom 20.0, $245,000) -- so this is explicitly the **new-player opening view**, not a late-game screen. Screenshot and full `state.json` are in the capture:

`%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\P(Doom)\flight_recorder\session_20260730_164411\`

Pip's note, verbatim and unedited, because it reads as a coherent brief rather than a bug list:

> "The vertical stack of buttons should be arranged such that the player doesn't need to scroll to see anything from a starting perspective. The upgrades on the right hand side need to have a vertical column to go up and down like the buttons on the left. We can try having them mirror the icon button stacks but with their vertical slice extending to the top of the screen as well, experiment with wireframing other locations, and consider what parts of the simulation we want to have persistently visible across both Plan and Watch screens, if any. If we don't want to put them on the Plan space, we should workshop UI improvements to the middle of the screen, which is wasted dead space. We can prioritise increasing legibility, particularly legibility for new players. The amount of scattered text over the screen is hard to read for older players, and more instructions should be more intuitive and we should have one more centralised location for text and not otherwise clutter the screen up too much with it. It's not obvious how to progress or end the turn, these things should be spelled out for new players explicitly within the first turn's setup / suggested setup."

## The distinct asks inside it

1. **No scrolling at the opening view.** The left button stack must fit without scrolling from a standing start.
2. **Upgrades need their own vertical column** on the right, scrollable like the left stack -- candidate treatment is mirroring the left icon stack with the vertical slice running to the top of the screen.
3. **Wireframe alternatives before committing.** Explicitly an experiment, not a chosen design.
4. **Decide what stays persistently visible across Plan and Watch.** This is a screen-architecture question, not a layout tweak, and it should be answered before (2) is built -- it changes what the columns are even for.
5. **The middle of the screen is wasted dead space.** Either it earns its area or the flanking columns should claim it. Pip flagged the same thing in the morning playtest: *"the buttons on the left-hand side of the screen I find was to have all this wasted space in the middle"* (#1041, [2:37]).
6. **Legibility first, new players first.** Scattered text across the whole screen is hard to read. Consolidate to fewer, more central text locations; stop cluttering.
7. **How to progress / end the turn is not obvious.** It should be stated explicitly in the first turn's setup or a suggested-setup flow.

## Why this is one issue rather than seven

Items 1, 2, 4 and 5 are all the same question -- what the Plan screen's columns are FOR, and therefore where they live and how wide they are. Fixing them piecemeal produces a layout that is locally better and globally incoherent. Item 4 in particular is upstream of the rest.

Items 6 and 7 are a separate axis (legibility and onboarding) but land on the same surface, so they should be designed together rather than sequentially.

## Related

- #1041 -- the morning playtest's UI findings, including the same dead-middle observation and the hiring/leaderboard screens wanting more room
- #1029 -- intro replay, needed to iterate on item 7 at all without deleting a config value by hand each time
- #814 -- progressive disclosure onboarding (operator monologue, greyed-UI intro, hire waterfall)
- #889 -- Architecture Week / `main_ui.gd` monolith, which is where a real layout rework would have to live

Not for the league. This is design work, and the note itself says "experiment" and "workshop".

## Process note

This capture is the first use of the F6 flight recorder as an actual feedback channel, and it worked exactly as intended: one keypress produced a screenshot, the full serialized game state, and a typed note, all timestamped together. Considerably better evidence than a video frame plus a transcript. Worth keeping as the standard for design observations, with recorded video reserved for things that need motion.

issues.title: Score payload: emit player name AND lab name, plus a dev-mode-used flag (website side is built)
issues.body:
Two asks from Pip, 2026-07-30, both needing the game to **emit** something the
website cannot derive. The website side is already built and merged-pending
(pdoom1-website PR #202) — it renders both the moment the payload carries them,
and renders exactly what it does today when it does not. **No website change is
needed after this lands, and no deploy has to race the release.**

## What the payload carries today

Read live off `https://api.pdoom1.com/score_api.php?seed=weekly-2026-w30&version=L3`:

```json
{"score":153,"doom_integral":10571,"player_name":"Applied AI Safety",
 "date":"2026-07-30T09:10:04","level_reached":153,"game_mode":"v0.13.2",
 "duration_seconds":475.814,"entry_uuid":"...","baseline_score":0,
 "baseline_doom_integral":0}
```

Two observations that shape both asks:

1. **There is exactly one identity slot, `player_name`, and the client puts the
   LAB name in it.** There is no human-name field at all. The website cannot
   split one string into two truths, so this is not fixable at our end.
2. **`game_mode` does not hold a game mode — it holds the build version**
   (`"v0.13.2"`). Worth knowing because it makes `game_mode` the cheapest
   available carrier for ask 2, and because the field name will mislead the next
   person who reads it.

## Ask 1 — player name AND lab name

Pip's words: *"My scores will be beaten rapidly. This is why I want my name
there."* An auto-generated lab name does not tell a visitor whose run it was,
and once the board fills up the Commissioner's own runs become anonymous.

**Either shape works — the website accepts both, pick whichever is cheaper:**

| Option | Payload | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **A (preferred)** | keep `player_name` = the human name, add **`lab_name`** | Semantically correct: the field called player_name holds the player. Requires the client to stop putting the lab in `player_name`. |
| **B** | leave `player_name` holding the lab, add **`player_handle`** | Zero risk to existing rows; nothing already stored changes meaning. Slightly wrong field names forever. |

Renders as `Pip — Applied AI Safety`, human name leading, lab quieter beside it.
With only one field present it renders exactly as it does now.

**Please confirm one thing I could not test without writing to production:** does
the PHP API **persist unknown fields**, or does it whitelist? If it whitelists,
a new field is silently dropped and both options are dead until the API changes
— which would make option C (the client packs `"Pip / Applied AI Safety"` into
`player_name` as a single string) the only thing that can ship this week. The
website renders option C fine, it just cannot style the two halves differently.

## Ask 2 — dev-mode-used indicator

Pip: *"we want the dev mode used indicator soon. Ladder integrity will probably
break this week, that's fine and expected."*

Only the game knows whether dev tooling was enabled during a run, so the website
can only render what it is told. **Two carriers accepted:**

- a boolean **`dev_mode`** field (clean), or
- a dev marker inside the existing free-form `game_mode` string, e.g.
  **`"v0.13.2-dev"`** — ships with **no schema change at all**, since that field
  is already a free-text version string.

Renders as a bordered `DEV BUILD` badge on the row, with hover text explaining
non-comparability rather than accusing anyone.

**The honesty constraint the website enforces, so you can rely on it:** an entry
*without* a marker is never labelled clean. Absence of the marker is not
evidence of absence — every entry set before the marker exists is unmarked too.
So the badge accumulates meaning going forward and never retroactively certifies
history. If you would rather it read `DEBUG` or `SANDBOX`, say so and I will
change the label.

## Ask 3 — say it in the patch notes

Pip wants players told that ladder integrity is expected to break this week.
That is the right call and I am doing the website half regardless. **The game
half is one paragraph in the v0.13.2 release notes** — it wants to come from the
game, since the game is what changed. Suggested substance, reword freely:

> This week's board is a deliberate mid-month fork. v0.13.2 runs on ladder epoch
> L3, and L3 changed the rules substantially — the action-point pool is gone in
> favour of an attention economy, office lease and lock-in are in, founder hours
> are four-way, six previously-inert upgrades are wired, and quirks are
> rebalanced. Scores set under the old rules are not comparable to scores set
> under these, which is exactly why the ladder version is a separate part of the
> board key. A small number of scores from before the fork are stranded and we
> are not merging them forward; merging scores earned under different rules
> would be the specific lie the ladder split exists to prevent.

The website will carry the same statement on `/leaderboard/` so a player who
never reads a release note still sees it.

## Timing

Neither ask blocks Friday. If either can ride the Friday re-cut, the board opens
with names on it, which is worth more on day one than on day eight. If not, Aug 7
(v0.14 / L4) is the natural home and the website needs no further work either way.

issues.title: playtest 2026-07-30 (v0.13.2 artifact): UI/UX findings from the Gate 4 run
issues.body:
Findings from Pip's recorded playtest of the **built 0.13.2 release artifact**, 2026-07-30 09:03, 9m06s. Transcript and frames in `art_generated/audiodump/` (gitignored).

The four league-critical ones were fixed same-day in PR #1039. **This issue holds the remainder** so they are scheduled rather than living in a recording nobody re-listens to -- the lesson of the pack-schema lane (#1018), which was never ticketed and therefore never happened.

Ordered by Pip's own emphasis, with timestamps so the audio can be checked.

## Nomenclature: "Turn" is counting days

**[1:44]** *"Stop having it fucking saying turn 21. It is either day 21 or the turn number is the number of like times we get into the planning mode."* And **[6:21]** *"Turn 133, that's wrong, I'm up to January 2018."*

The top-left counter increments per day, but is labelled Turn. Under the current model a turn is a planning cycle, not a day. This is a semantic fix with real surface area (the label, the tooltip, anything that reads it, and probably the leaderboard's "Turns" column, which per #1039 does correctly mean score). Wants a ruling on what a turn IS before any renaming. Related: #1037, and `docs/GLOSSARY.md` should carry the answer.

## Hiring and onboarding

- **[2:11]** The hiring pipeline screen needs to be roughly **double its size** -- "so we can see everything".
- **[2:21]** Hiring actions stack in the in-flight section but **do not create cards in the action queue**. Pip wants both, so priorities can be seen and rearranged.
- **[5:07]** The onboarding prompt fires only on the **offer -> accept** path. Other hiring routes complete with no prompt, and nothing directs the player to the onboarding section at all.
- **[5:37]** Make the hiring pipeline a more significant UI feature, easier to navigate in and out of. Same for the liability ledger.

## Screens that need more room

- **[6:51]** The global-leaderboard one-time-choice screen and the defeat screen should both be **about twice as big** -- information is being lost while dead space sits behind them.
- **[7:15]** Grey out the take-more-actions buttons until score submission is **confirmed**, not merely started.
- **[7:27]** The "press Enter for leaderboard" prompt is **below the fold** -- it needs scrolling to discover.

## Leaderboard presentation (beyond the #1039 column fix)

- **[7:36]** Default view is **local**; it should probably be **global**.
- **[7:54]** Player name and lab name display still need work.
- **[8:17]** **Highlight the viewer's own entry** with a horizontal band -- otherwise it is undifferentiated text.
- **[8:31]** Add **ABAB row striping** and **vertical grid lines**, applied through the colour schema so they stay consistent when the palette changes.

## Visual homes for two systems

**[5:47]** Both should stay greyed out in-game until they have a proper introduction -- a transition or scene, not a bare panel appearing:
- **Liability ledger** -- "a scribbled bit of paper... with an IOU at the top" as the basic version.
- **Onboarding pipeline** -- possibly a whiteboard. Background undecided.

The mobile phone already serves this role for the bank, so the pattern exists.

## Smaller

- **[0:13]** The What's New modal says **no patch notes available** for this version. First thing a player sees on a league build. `godot/data/patch_notes.json` has no 0.13.2 entry.
- **[0:19]** The dev-build badge (top right) is clipped; needs to move left to be readable.
- **[1:11]** A cat portrait renders as a magenta/black pattern at high doom. **Not** a missing texture -- verified the textures are in the `.pck` (`arwen` appears 8 times, 1004 `.ctex` entries). Likely a doom-level modulate. Pip: "not so much [a priority] but it's solveable".
- **[1:27]** The strategic-moves-unlocked popup needs a header, and is hardcoded to a fixed time.
- **[2:48]** Images spill over text in several panels.
- **[4:59]** Fundraising results resolve too fast -- wants them slowed.

## Already tracked elsewhere, listed so nobody re-files

Action queue overflow, leaderboard column off-by-one, the F8/N key, and the feed placeholder are all **fixed in #1039**. Placeholder convention is #1031; AP vocabulary is #1037; the intro replay Pip needs for repeat playtesting is #1029.

issues.title: macOS HOW-TO-RUN still tells testers to right-click -> Open, which Sequoia 15.x removed
issues.body:
Filed from the pdoom1-website side during league week, 2026-07-30 ~0900, because
website issue #199 / PR #195 corrected this exact instruction on the site
yesterday and the correction did not reach this repo.

## The stale line

`tools/release_notes/HOW-TO-RUN-macos.txt:6-8` reads:

```
2. First launch: right-click (or Control-click) P(Doom).app -> Open ->
   Open. A plain double-click may be blocked by Gatekeeper because the
   build is unsigned / not notarized (alpha).
```

**Apple removed that path in macOS Sequoia 15.x.** The right-click → Open
override no longer appears in the Finder context menu for an unsigned,
un-notarised app. A tester on 15.x who follows step 2 finds no such menu item
and concludes the download is broken.

The file already carries the working instruction at step 3 (`xattr -dr
com.apple.quarantine`). **This is an ordering defect, not a missing fix** —
step 3 needs to be step 2 for 15.x, and the right-click path needs a version
label.

## What I could NOT verify — please check before deciding urgency

`grep -rniE "release_notes|HOW-TO-RUN"` across this repo returns **no consumer**.
Neither `tools/build_release.py` nor `.github/workflows/enhanced-release.yml`
references `tools/release_notes/`. So one of two things is true, and I cannot
tell which from the outside:

- **It ships via a manual step.** Then a Sequoia tester is being actively
  walked into a wall, and the fix wants to land before the export finishes,
  because after that it is a re-cut rather than an edit.
- **It is orphaned.** Then nothing is broken today, but the file is a decoy
  that reads as authoritative and will be trusted the next time someone
  assembles a zip by hand.

Both cases take the same one-line-order fix, so the fix is cheap either way;
only the deadline differs.

## Suggested replacement for steps 2-3

```
2. First launch on macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later: macOS will refuse the app and
   offer no override in the Finder menu. Clear the quarantine flag from
   Terminal instead:
      xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "P(Doom).app"
   Then double-click normally. You may be asked for your admin password.

3. On macOS 14 and earlier: right-click (or Control-click) P(Doom).app ->
   Open -> Open. This path was removed by Apple in Sequoia, which is why
   step 2 exists.
```

Wording is aligned with what the website now serves at
`public/index.html:911-930` (pdoom1-website PR #195, merged 2026-07-29), so the
zip and the download page tell a Mac tester the same story.

## One more instance, upstream of the website

The **v0.13.1 GitHub release body** also carries `macOS Gatekeeper: right-click
-> Open the first time`. The website republishes that body verbatim via
`public/data/version.json`, and pdoom1-website PR #183 renders release notes on
`/game-changelog/`, so the dead instruction reaches readers through a second
door the website cannot fix at its end. **Please keep it out of the v0.13.2
notes.**

## Bearing on the gate rail

Not Gate 4 blocking on my read — Gate 4 proves the artifact runs, and this is a
text file inside it. Flagging it now rather than Friday because the Thursday
morning window is the last point where it is an edit instead of a re-cut, and
because Thursday ~1700's cold playtest is the only scheduled test by someone
who would actually follow the instructions as written.

issues.title: trust: make provable declarations about what the game touches -- exit surfaces, provenance, signing
issues.body:
Raised 2026-07-30 from a real reaction. A friend of Pip's was **hesitant to run the game at all**, because they could not tell what an LLM-assisted codebase might have put in a binary. That is a reasonable position and it will become more common, not less.

Pip's instinct, verbatim:

> "I think we should also be able to make reasonably provably true declarations about what the game impacts on its exit surfaces, right? just generating text files etc. I built it to be pretty non-intrusive in my early thinking."

That instinct is the right one and it is worth cashing in, because the claim happens to be true and is currently undocumented.

## The honest ceiling, stated up front

**You cannot prove the absence of vulnerabilities.** No scan does that, and claiming otherwise to a technical audience destroys the credibility the exercise is meant to build. The achievable goal is a **chain of verifiable evidence** that makes doubt cheap to resolve. Everything below is judged against that standard, not against "proof".

## What the concern actually is

Very likely NOT a deliberate backdoor. The real risks in LLM-assisted code are:

1. **Unvetted dependencies** -- something pulled in that nobody audited.
2. **Accidental exposure** -- an overshared telemetry field, a permissive write, a committed secret.
3. **Unsigned binaries** -- nobody can distinguish what you built from what someone else modified.

Addressing these three specifically is far more convincing than a general reassurance.

## The exit-surface declaration (Pip's idea, and the cheapest high-value item)

A short, plain-English, **auditable** statement of everything the program touches, published with each release. Known surfaces to enumerate and verify:

- **Network out:** leaderboard score submit and board fetch, the launch ping, the update check. Name the exact hosts and what each payload contains.
- **Filesystem:** writes confined to Godot's `user://` (`%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\P(Doom)\`) -- config, logs, screenshots, local leaderboard JSON. No writes outside it.
- **What it does NOT do:** no installer, no registry writes, no admin elevation, no background service, no persistence after exit.

Each line must be **checkable against the source**, and the doc should say how to check it. A statement that cannot be verified is just a nicer-sounding assurance.

## Ranked by how much doubt each removes

1. **Code signing + notarization** (#683, #917). Biggest single move. Does not prove safety -- attaches an accountable real identity, and stops the OS presenting the build as suspicious. Right now an unsigned build is indistinguishable from a tampered one, which is the actual problem.
2. **Build provenance attestation.** `actions/attest-build-provenance` in the release workflow proves artifact X was built from public commit Y. This is the direct answer to "what did the LLM put in there": the source is readable and the binary provably came from it.
3. **Publish artifact SHA256 + a VirusTotal link per release.** Cheap, and checkable in thirty seconds by a non-specialist.
4. **The exit-surface declaration above.**
5. **Dependency and secret scanning** -- `pip-audit` on the Python tooling (dev-surface only; the shipped artifact contains no Python), gitleaks alongside the existing `detect-private-key` pre-commit hook.

## Two technical distinctions to get right

**Memory leaks here are not a security issue.** GDScript is memory-managed; a leak means orphaned nodes, which is a stability concern. The suite already surfaces it (`ObjectDB instances leaked at exit`, GUT orphan counts). Exploitable memory corruption would live in Godot's C++ engine -- not this codebase, and far more scrutinised than anything written here. Conflating the two overstates risk in one direction and understates it in the other.

**The real native surface is the GDExtension.** GDScript is not native code; the godotsteam GDExtension binary is. Pin it by version and hash, and say so.

## Worth checking while doing this

CLAUDE.md states Godot packs the **entire** `godot/` tree into the `.pck`, which implies `addons/gut` -- the test framework -- ships inside the 58 MB player build. Dead code in a shipped artifact and unnecessary surface. Confirm and strip if so.

## Relationship to #1027

Same principle, pointed outward. #1027 is about the project detecting its own silent wrongness; this is about a stranger being able to verify the artifact without trusting anyone. Both replace assurance with evidence.

Not for this week. Candidate: alongside the signing work, which it naturally pairs with.

issues.title: nomenclature: stale 'AP' vocabulary in player-facing text after the attention-economy migration (#996) -- scoped sweep + GLOSSARY.md is missing
issues.body:
Raised by Pip while playtesting 2026-07-30, verbatim:

> "still called AP in the dialogues in game, we should start sweeping for that, maybe as a wider nomenclature and player facing text drive?"

The AP (Action Points) pool was REMOVED on 2026-07-28 (#996) and replaced by
founder **Attention** plus typed founder hours (planning / operating). The code
migrated. The words did not.

This is not a find-and-replace ticket. `AP` -> `Attention` is wrong in several
places, because some of the surviving text describes a *mechanic* that no longer
exists, not just a *noun* that was renamed. And a third bucket must never be
touched at all.

## Bucket 1 -- PLAYER-FACING and WRONG (these are the ones that matter)

Text a player reads describing a mechanic that no longer exists. All verified as
NOT overwritten by runtime code unless noted.

### Event dialogue -- Pip's actual complaint

| Location | String | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd:78` | `parts.append("%d AP" % int(amount))` | The branch guard immediately above is `elif resource == "attention":`. The engine already speaks Attention; the label says AP. |
| `godot/scripts/ui/event_dialog.gd:257` | `missing_resources.append("AP (need %s, have %s available)" % [cost, available])` | Same -- inside `if resource == "attention":`. This is the "you cannot afford this" message. |

These two are literally "the code says attention, the player reads AP". Highest
confidence, most visible, cheapest fix.

### In-game help (teaches the wrong model outright)

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn:125` | `Actions cost Action Points (AP) and resources` |
| `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn:184` | `6. [b]Action Points:[/b] Use all your AP each turn - wasted AP = wasted time` |

`:184` is worse than stale vocabulary -- it teaches a *strategy* ("use all your
AP each turn") for a resource that no longer exists, in a system where unspent
reserve evaporates at month end and the binding constraint is the planning /
operating hour split.

### Main screen chrome

| Location | String | Liveness |
|---|---|---|
| `godot/scenes/main.tscn:355` | `text = "Reserve AP"` (ReserveAPButton) | **LIVE.** `main_ui.gd:1175,1191` only touch `.disabled`; the text is never reassigned. |
| `godot/scenes/main.tscn:376` | `tooltip_text = "Execute queued actions and advance to next turn. Shows warning if you have unused AP."` | **LIVE.** `main_ui.gd:407` overwrites the button's `.text` to `COMMIT THE MONTH >` but never its `tooltip_text`. So the button says "commit the month" and its tooltip says "advance to next turn ... unused AP". |

### Feed / log lines the player reads

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:868` | `log_message("[color=cyan]Reserving 1 AP for events...[/color]")` |
| `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:893` | `log_message("[color=yellow]Action queue cleared - AP refunded[/color]")` |
| `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:903` | `log_message("[color=yellow]Removed: %s (+%d AP)[/color]" % [action_name, ap_cost])` -- note the value it prints comes from `result.get("attention_cost", 0)` |

### Plan screen

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/ui/plan_controller.gd:138` | `"name": "Reserve All AP"` |
| `godot/scripts/ui/plan_controller.gd:139` | `"description": "No planned actions - keep all AP available for responding to events"` |

The docstring three lines above (`:132`) already says "hold all Attention for
response windows". The surrounding prose migrated; the player-visible strings
did not.

### Travel / conference panel

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd:519` | `submit_btn.text = "Submit Paper (1 AP)"` |
| `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd:615` | `cost_label.text = "... \nTotal: %s + 2 AP"` |
| `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd:638` | `attend_btn.text = "Attend (2 AP)"` |

### Content data

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/data/historical_timeline/2017.json:108` | `"text": "Organize safety reading group (costs 2 AP)"` |
| `godot/data/historical_timeline/2017.json:148` | `"text": "Integrate principles into lab policy (costs 2 AP, $10k)"` |

Loaded by `godot/scripts/data/timeline_loader.gd:14`
(`res://data/historical_timeline`). These are choice labels -- player-read, and
they assert a specific cost in a retired unit.

### Upgrade catalogue

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/core/upgrades.gd:68` | `"description": "Auto-orders supplies when low (maintains stationery without AP cost)"` |

### Keybind UI

| Location | String |
|---|---|
| `godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd:72` | `"commit_plan": {..., "description": "Commit Plan & Reserve AP"}` -- surfaced in the keybind/settings screen. See also #1011 (three docs already disagree with this file). |

**Bucket 1 total: 18 strings across 9 files.**

### Boot-failure-only, listed for completeness, NOT bucket 1

Two `main.tscn` lines say AP but are overwritten in normal play, so a player only
sees them if boot fails (i.e. #1023's failure mode):

- `godot/scenes/main.tscn:176` -- `text = "AP: 0"`, overwritten at
  `main_ui.gd:1112` with `Attention: %d (%d free, %d queued)`.
- `godot/scenes/main.tscn:177` -- `tooltip_text = "Action Points. Limits actions
  per turn. Base 3 + 0.5 per staff."`, overwritten at `main_ui.gd:1116` with the
  real Attention/hours tooltip.

Correcting a claim made when this was reported: `:177` is **not** live
player-facing text. It is still wrong and still describes removed mechanics
("Base 3 + 0.5 per staff" is exactly the dead pool formula), and it is on the
list -- it just belongs with the placeholder-sentinel work, not with the
player-facing sweep. Both lines are already in `docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md`'s DANGEROUS table and are owned by #1031.

## Bucket 2 -- DEVELOPER-FACING (lower priority, still worth doing)

Dev overlays, debug strings, docstrings, identifiers. No player ever reads these;
they cost comprehension time for anyone (human or agent) reading the code.

| Location | Kind |
|---|---|
| `godot/scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd:347` | `"Debug: Added 5 AP"` |
| `godot/scenes/debug_overlay.tscn:98` | `text = "Add 5 Action Points"` |
| `godot/scripts/debug/dev_mode_readout.gd:52` | `"AP: %d total \| %d avail \| %d committed \| %d reserved"` |
| `godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:322` | docstring `"""Purchase an upgrade - doesn't consume AP"""` |
| `godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:432` | docstring `"""Remove specific action from queue and refund its AP cost"""` |

Plus identifiers throughout: `ap_label`, `ap_cost`, `ap_text`, `ap_color_name`,
`reserve_ap()` (`game_manager.gd:385`), `_on_reserve_ap_button_pressed()`
(`main_ui.gd:866`), and the scene node names `APLabel`
(`godot/scenes/main.tscn:173`) and `ReserveAPButton`
(`godot/scenes/main.tscn:353`).

**Warning on the node names specifically:** renaming `APLabel` /
`ReserveAPButton` breaks `@onready var ap_label = $TopBar/APLabel`
(`main_ui.gd:13`), `$BottomBar/ControlButtons/ReserveAPButton`
(`main_ui.gd:39`), and the `[connection]` at `godot/scenes/main.tscn:418`. It
also requires editing `.tscn` files, which is off-limits during a freeze and is
pure churn. Recommend: rename identifiers and node names as a **separate,
post-league, single-purpose PR** or not at all. Do not bundle it with the
player-facing sweep -- mixing a risky rename into a text fix is how a cosmetic PR
becomes a regression.

`godot/tests/**` contributes a further 18 quoted-string AP hits. Same bucket,
lowest priority; they should follow whatever the identifiers do.

## Bucket 3 -- HISTORICAL and CORRECT: DO NOT SWEEP

**Changing any of these falsifies the record.** Anyone running a
search-and-replace must exclude them explicitly.

| Location | Why it must stay |
|---|---|
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:26` | `"AP Double-Spend Bug - Actions no longer deduct AP twice"` -- describes what an old version did. |
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:30` | `"Event Popup AP Display - Shows correct available AP"` |
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:52` | `"Event AP Logic uses available AP correctly"` |
| `godot/data/patch_notes.json:56` | `"Turn Philosophy: 'Skip Turn' renamed to 'Commit Plan & Reserve AP'"` |
| `godot/data/balance/defaults.json:15` | `_description` states "as of T2 (2026-07-28) no legacy AP pool either: Attention is the ONLY founder currency". This is the correct, current, explanatory text -- it uses "AP" precisely to say the AP pool is gone. |
| `godot/scripts/core/actions.gd:552` | comment quoting the workshop ruling verbatim: `"staff never add founder AP"` |
| `godot/scripts/core/turn_manager.gd:87` | same quotation: `"the pool illusion dies; staff never add founder AP"` |
| `godot/scripts/core/office.gd:18` | quotes #791: `"predictable AP/cash sink"` |

The last three are **verbatim quotations of design rulings**. Editing the words
inside a quotation to match current vocabulary makes the citation false. If they
bother anyone, the correct treatment is to leave the quote intact and add a
bracketed gloss outside it, not to rewrite it.

## Bucket counts

| Bucket | Strings | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 1 -- player-facing and WRONG | 18 | 9 |
| 1b -- boot-failure-only (goes with the placeholder work) | 2 | 1 |
| 2 -- developer-facing strings | 5 | 3 (+ identifiers, + 18 test strings) |
| 3 -- historical, DO NOT TOUCH | 8 | 5 |

Raw totals for reference: `\bAP\b|Action Points?` matches 100 lines in
`godot/**/*.gd`, 7 in `godot/**/*.json`, 7 in `godot/**/*.tscn`. Most of the
`.gd` volume is identifiers and tests.

## Why this is a nomenclature drive, not a replace

Pip's instinct ("maybe as a wider nomenclature and player facing text drive?") is
the right frame, for a concrete reason visible in the table: several bucket-1
strings cannot be fixed by substituting a word.

- `player_guide.tscn:184` "Use all your AP each turn - wasted AP = wasted time"
  needs rewriting around the monthly grant, evaporating reserve, and the
  planning/operating split. There is no word that makes that sentence true.
- `main.tscn:376`'s tooltip says "advance to next turn" on a button labelled
  `COMMIT THE MONTH >`. The turn-vs-month vocabulary drifted separately from AP.
- `main.tscn:177` (boot-failure-only) states a formula, `Base 3 + 0.5 per staff`.
- "Reserve AP" as a *concept* still exists (holding Attention for response
  windows) but "reserve" may not be the right word for it any more -- that is a
  design call, not a text call.

So the sweep needs a decided vocabulary first, applied second. Which raises:

## Blocker: `docs/GLOSSARY.md` does not exist

CONFIRMED. `find . -iname "*glossary*"` over the repo returns nothing. Two
documents already reference it as though it does:

- `docs/art/ENDGAME_CONCEPT_REVIEW_2026-07-29.md:339` -- "Consider adding A9
  (poster art vs hero art) to `docs/GLOSSARY.md`"
- `docs/game-design/WS3_ENDGAME_RULINGS_2026-07-29.md:130` -- "Add the
  escalation-ladder vocabulary to `docs/GLOSSARY.md`; cross-index it"

This is #1027's pattern again, and #1018's: documents referring confidently to
things that are not there. The glossary needs to be created and to state
authoritatively what the current terms are -- Attention, planning hours,
operating hours, month vs turn vs day, reserve -- before a text sweep has
anything to sweep *toward*. That should probably be step 0 of this issue rather
than a separate ticket.

## Suggested sequence

1. Create `docs/GLOSSARY.md` with the current founder-economy vocabulary
   (Attention, planning/operating hours, monthly grant, reserve/evaporation) and
   the turn/month/day time model. Source of truth: `godot/data/balance/defaults.json:15`
   `_description`, ADR-0009/0011, and `main_ui.gd:1116`'s Attention tooltip,
   which is currently the single best plain-English statement of the mechanic in
   the repo.
2. Fix the two `event_dialog.gd` strings (`:78`, `:257`). Two lines, highest
   visibility, directly answers Pip's report.
3. Fix the remaining 16 bucket-1 strings, rewriting rather than substituting
   where the sentence describes dead mechanics.
4. Bucket 2 strings.
5. Identifiers and node names -- separate PR, post-league, or never.
6. Never touch bucket 3.

## League relevance

Steps 2 and 3 touch player-visible text in a build shipping Friday. They are
string-only changes with no logic or balance impact, so they are low-risk if
someone wants them in the cut -- but note that step 3 includes edits to
`godot/scenes/main.tscn` and `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn`, which is scene
churn during a freeze. My read: **step 2 is worth taking (two `.gd` string
literals, near-zero risk, fixes the thing the tester actually noticed); steps 3+
should wait for the cut.** That is a call for Pip, not for me.

Related: #996 (the AP pool removal that stranded this vocabulary), #1011 (keybind
docs already disagree with `keybind_manager.gd`), #1018, #1027, and #1031 (owns `main.tscn:176-177`).

issues.title: testing: which tests pass only by alphabetical ordering accident? GameManager autoload leaks between files

labels.name: testing
labels.description: Issues related to test suite and testing infrastructure

issues.body:
Surfaced while reviewing the new boot-liveness test written for #1023. The test
itself is fine -- it is the *reason* it needed a particular piece of teardown
that is the finding.

## The concrete evidence (CONFIRMED)

`godot/tests/unit/test_boot_produces_live_run.gd:66-72`:
```
func after_all() -> void:
	# Hand the autoload back VIRGIN, not live. This file sorts first in tests/unit, and
	# test_game_start_actionable.gd's `assert_true(gm.is_initialized)` is only meaningful when
	# it starts from an un-initialized autoload -- leaving a live run here would silently make
	# that older guard vacuous. Restoring engine-start state keeps every later file seeing
	# exactly the environment it saw before this file existed.
	_make_autoload_virgin()
```

`_make_autoload_virgin()` at `:75-89` nulls `GameManager.state`, `turn_manager`,
`month_controller`, sets `is_initialized = false`, and calls
`_release_game_objects()` first (because `GameState`/`DoomSystem`/`RiskPool`/
`TurnManager` extend `Node` and are never in the tree, so nulling without
freeing leaks 4 orphans and trips `test_game_lifecycle_hygiene.gd`'s global
orphan-count assertion).

The assertion it is protecting:
`godot/tests/unit/test_game_start_actionable.gd:61` --
`assert_true(gm.is_initialized, "GameManager must be initialized after auto-init")`.

## The actual finding -- read this rather than the fix

`GameManager` is an **autoload** (`godot/project.godot`
`GameManager="*res://scripts/game_manager.gd"`). Since L0 (#620/#608) the
autoload singleton IS the one GameManager -- `dev_mode_overlay.gd:34-41`
documents that both resolution branches return the same live instance. So
process-global state persists across every test file in a GUT run.

That means `assert_true(gm.is_initialized)` in
`test_game_start_actionable.gd` has been passing **whether or not the boot path
under test did anything**, for as long as any earlier-sorting file left the
autoload live. It has been meaningful only by accident of alphabetical file
ordering -- and the new file's `after_all` preserves that accident deliberately
rather than removing the dependency.

`test_boot_produces_live_run.gd` handles its own exposure correctly: its class
doc at `:20-25` names the hazard, and every test in it drives the autoload to a
known state first and asserts **differentially** -- on state object IDENTITY, not
truthiness (`:207`). That is the pattern that actually works. It is applied in
exactly one file.

## The real question this raises

**Which other tests are only passing by ordering accident?**

Nobody knows, and that is the finding. This is the #640 family exactly: a gate
reporting green while not actually exercising what it claims (there, zero tests
ran; here, assertions run but cannot fail). #1027's table calls this the
project's dominant failure mode -- silent wrongness that looks right -- and a
green suite is the highest-trust surface in the repo.

Candidate audit surface: 10 test files under `godot/tests/unit/` reference the
`GameManager` autoload directly.

```
tests/unit/test_action_bar_renderer.gd
tests/unit/test_adaptive_music.gd
tests/unit/test_boot_produces_live_run.gd      (already handles it)
tests/unit/test_game_lifecycle_hygiene.gd
tests/unit/test_game_start_actionable.gd       (confirmed vulnerable)
tests/unit/test_hiring_panel_controller.gd
tests/unit/test_save_load_roundtrip.gd
tests/unit/test_ui_scene_reentry_safety.gd
tests/unit/simulation/test_adversarial_ui_state.gd
tests/unit/simulation/test_month_controller.gd
```

Other process-global autoloads worth the same treatment: `GameConfig`
(`pending_load_path` is already save/restored per-test in the boot file at
`:60-61`, which is a hint that others may not be), `EventService`, `Balance`,
`Achievements`, `VerificationTracker`.

## Suggested approach (options, not a mandate)

**A. Mutation-style spot check, cheap and decisive.** For each suspect assertion,
temporarily break the thing it claims to verify and confirm the test goes red.
Manual, an hour or two, and it produces a definitive list rather than a
suspicion. This is what I would do first.

**B. Randomise test file order in CI.** GUT would need to support it (unverified
whether it does). Ordering-dependent tests then fail intermittently -- which
surfaces the class but converts a silent problem into a flaky one. Only useful
alongside A.

**C. Structural fix: a shared autoload-reset helper** that every test touching a
global autoload calls in `before_all`, rather than each file being responsible
for cleaning up after itself. This inverts the current contract, which is
"leave the world as you found it" -- fine in principle but it fails open (a file
that forgets to clean up damages *later* files, and the damage is invisible).
"Establish the world you need" fails closed. Note `test_boot_produces_live_run.gd`
already does both: it establishes its own preconditions AND restores on exit.
Making that the house pattern is the durable answer.

**D. Standardise on differential assertions.** `assert_true(x.is_initialized)`
is weak against any global; `assert_ne(state_before, state_after)` on object
identity is not. Cheap review-level rule, no tooling.

Recommendation: A to find out how bad it is, then C+D as the standing pattern.
B only if GUT makes it free.

## Housekeeping note

`godot/tests/unit/test_boot_produces_live_run.gd` is currently **untracked** in
the working tree (`git status` shows `??`). It needs to be committed before any
of this reasoning is durable -- and the `after_all` teardown must survive review,
because without it `test_game_start_actionable.gd:61` becomes vacuous the moment
the new file lands.

Related: #640 (CI green while running zero tests), #1023 (the boot failure that prompted the new test), #1026, #1027 (point 2, "same-path testing"), #1031 (same silent-wrongness family, UI side).

issues.title: ascii(#744): player-facing non-ASCII survives in .tscn text -- check_no_emoji.py only blocks emoji there
issues.body:
The repo has a hard ASCII-only rule (#744), enforced for `.gd` and `.json` by the
blocking `no-emoji` pre-commit hook. `.tscn` is deliberately exempted from the
ASCII half of that check -- and player-facing non-ASCII has accumulated in the
gap.

## Evidence (CONFIRMED)

`scripts/check_no_emoji.py:76` applies the `ord(ch) > 0x7F` test only to
`.gd`/`.json`. For `.tscn` it calls `scan_emoji()` (`:100`), which tests
`is_emoji()` (`:34-44`) -- emoji blocks and variation selectors only. The
rationale is written into the file at `:10-11`: "godot/**/*.tscn may contain
engine-serialized unicode that must not be touched". That rationale is sound for
engine-serialized data; it currently also covers authored `text = ` strings,
which it should not.

Full survey of `godot/**/*.tscn` (excluding `addons/`): **11 lines across 3
files**, all in authored strings, all above U+007F:

| Location | Codepoint | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `godot/scenes/leaderboard_screen.tscn:175` | U+2190 | `text = "<- Previous"` written with a real left arrow |
| `godot/scenes/leaderboard_screen.tscn:185` | U+2192 | `text = "Next ->"` written with a real right arrow |
| `godot/scenes/main.tscn:104` | U+2014 | `tooltip_text = "Turn counter [em-dash] number of workdays elapsed this run."` |
| `godot/scenes/main.tscn:270` | U+00B7 | `text = "Buy time [middot] survival is the score \| Lose: P(Doom) = 100%"` |
| `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn:124-127` | U+2022 | four bullet lines in the player guide prose |
| `godot/scenes/player_guide.tscn:154-156` | U+25CF | `Green dots (*)` / `Red dots (*)` / `Blue dots (*)` -- black-circle glyph |

(The table renders the offending characters as ASCII descriptions on purpose --
this issue body is itself ASCII-only.)

Every one of these is player-visible text. `main.tscn:270` is the tagline on the
main screen. `player_guide.tscn` is the in-game help.

Note `main.tscn:104` is a `tooltip_text` on `TurnCountLabel` -- the same node
whose `text` is dead per the placeholder audit. Both go away together if that
node is deleted.

## Why it matters, honestly

Two arguments, of different strengths:

- **Consistency with a stated hard rule (strong).** #744 says ASCII-only,
  em-dashes as `--`, bullets as `-`/`*`, arrows as `->`. The house chrome style
  is `[M]`, `>>`, `[ESC] close`, `[OK]`. These 11 lines are the only place
  player-facing text disagrees with the style the rest of the game uses, so the
  UI is internally inconsistent, not just rule-violating.
- **Font/encoding risk (weak, do not oversell).** U+2022, U+25CF, U+2190/2192,
  U+2014 and U+00B7 are all well-covered by any reasonable font, and Godot
  handles UTF-8 `.tscn` fine. I would put the probability of a visible tofu box
  for a player on a normal Windows/macOS/Linux setup at under 5%. This is a
  consistency and rule-integrity problem, not a rendering emergency. Anyone
  arguing it as a crash risk is overstating it.

## Enforcement constraint -- the inline-annotation trick does NOT transfer

Recorded so whoever picks this up does not rediscover it:
**Godot rewrites `.tscn` on save and drops comments.** The
`# scene-nav-allow` annotation used by `tools/check_scene_nav.py` cannot be used
in `.tscn`. Any allowlist for a `.tscn` gate must be an **external checked-in
file** (e.g. `tools/tscn_nonascii_allowlist.txt`, entries of the form
`path/to/scene.tscn:LINE` or `:NodePath`). Same constraint applies to the placeholder-sentinel gate proposed in #1031, so the two gates should probably share one allowlist mechanism.

## Options

**A. Fix the 11 lines, leave the checker alone.** Zero tooling. The gap reopens
the next time someone types a smart quote in the Godot editor.

**B. Fix the 11 lines, then extend `check_no_emoji.py` to apply the ASCII test to
`.tscn` values on `text = ` / `tooltip_text = ` / `placeholder_text = ` lines
only** (leaving engine-serialized fields, resource paths and binary-ish
properties alone, which is the exemption's actual purpose). Narrow, matches the
original intent, and the current violation count would be zero on arrival --
which is the right time to add a gate. Recommended.

**C. Full ASCII on all `.tscn` content.** Rejected: it would fight the engine's
own serialization, which is exactly what `check_no_emoji.py:10-11` was written to
avoid.

Order matters, same as the placeholder gate: fix first, gate second. A gate that
is red on arrival gets `--no-verify`-ed and then ignored.

## Priority

Minor. 11 lines, all cosmetic, none broken. Worth doing because it is small and
because a hard rule with a known hole is worse than a soft rule. Not
league-blocking, though the `.tscn` text edits themselves are trivially safe if
someone wants them in the Friday build -- they touch no logic.

Surfaced as a side finding in `docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md`.

Related: #744 (the ASCII rule), #743 (the theme lane that owns the remaining
`.tscn` exclusions in `check_no_emoji.py`), #1031 (the placeholder-sentinel gate, which shares the external-allowlist constraint).

issues.title: scene_transition (latent): fade transition awaits a pausable tween -- would deadlock ALL navigation if called while paused
issues.body:
**Not currently reachable.** Filing it as a defensive fix because the failure
mode is total and silent, the trigger is one ordinary-looking call away, and the
fix is one line.

## The mechanism (CONFIRMED from source, INFERRED for the pause semantics)

`godot/autoload/scene_transition.gd`:

- `:1` -- `extends CanvasLayer`. Registered as an autoload in
  `godot/project.godot`, with **no `process_mode` override** anywhere in the
  file. Grep over `godot/autoload/*.gd` finds only `leaderboard_sync.gd:49` and
  `update_check.gd:67` setting one. So SceneTransition inherits, i.e. pausable.
- `:97-99` -- if a fade was requested:
  ```
  if _pending_fade:
      fade_rect.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
      await fade_out()
  ```
- `:117-120` -- `fade_out()` is `create_tween()` +
  `tween_property(...)` + `await tween.finished`.

INFERRED (Godot semantics, not verified by running): a tween created via
`Node.create_tween()` is bound to that node and inherits its pause behaviour. On
a pausable node with `get_tree().paused == true`, the tween does not advance, so
`tween.finished` never emits, so `await fade_out()` never returns.

Consequence if it ever happens: `_run_transition()` suspends forever at `:99`.
`is_transitioning` is never cleared (it is set at `:60`/`:75` and only released
at `:113`, past the await). Every subsequent `go_to()` and `reload()` hits the
guard at `:55-57` / `:71-73` and returns early with a `push_warning`. **All
navigation for the rest of the session is silently dropped** -- no crash, no
player-visible error, buttons that simply stop doing anything. The user quits and
files "the menu buttons stopped working".

Also note `fade_rect.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` at `:98` is set
before the await and only reset at `:107`, so the full-screen rect would also
keep eating mouse input. The screen would be black and inert.

## Why it is not reachable today

Fade is opt-in. Every current caller of a fading transition:

- `godot/autoload/scene_transition.gd:83` -- `change_scene()` back-compat alias
  (`go_to(target_scene, true)`)
- `godot/scripts/ui/conference_vignette.gd:241`
- `godot/scripts/ui/travel_panel_controller.gd:426`

None of those runs while the tree is paused. The one place that navigates out of
a paused state -- `godot/scripts/ui/pause_menu.gd:70-73` -- sets
`get_tree().paused = false` **before** calling
`SceneTransition.go_to("res://scenes/welcome.tscn")`, and calls it without fade.
That ordering is currently load-bearing and nothing enforces it.

Trigger conditions, any one of which is enough: someone adds `, true` to the
pause menu's exit-to-menu call for a nicer transition; someone routes a
game-over or quit-confirm through a fade while paused; someone adds a fading
navigation to the dev overlay (which, per the separate ESC/dev-overlay issue, may
soon become always-processing while paused).

## Fix

One line in `_ready()`:

```
process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS
```

SceneTransition is a navigation router with no gameplay state, no RNG, and no
scoring involvement (its own class doc at `:1-21` is explicit that it never
touches state). It has no business being pausable. This also makes the pause
menu's ordering dependency stop mattering.

Add a regression test asserting `SceneTransition.process_mode ==
PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, or the fix is one careless refactor from being reverted.

## Priority

Latent. Zero player impact today. Cheap enough that it should just go in the next
time this file is touched -- but NOT during the Friday freeze, since it changes
the process semantics of the one autoload every screen transition passes through,
and the payoff is protection against a bug nobody can currently trigger. Land it
after the cut.

Related: #1033 (the `is_transitioning` release timing -- same file, same `_run_transition`), #1028 (same root-cause class: pausable nodes that should not be), #1027.

issues.title: scene_transition: is_transitioning released before the engine swaps; scene_load perf section excludes _ready
issues.body:
Found while auditing the scene-navigation chokepoint. Two related observations,
both about the same misalignment: `_run_transition()` treats
`change_scene_to_file()` as if it completed synchronously, and it does not.

## 1. The re-entrancy guard does not cover the whole transition

CONFIRMED from `godot/autoload/scene_transition.gd`:

- `:55-57` / `:71-73` -- `go_to()` and `reload()` drop a second request while
  `is_transitioning` is true.
- `:100-103` -- the swap itself:
  ```
  if _pending_reload:
      get_tree().reload_current_scene()
  else:
      get_tree().change_scene_to_file(_pending_target)
  ```
- `:113` -- `is_transitioning = false`, at the end of `_run_transition()`.

INFERRED from Godot semantics (not verified by running): `change_scene_to_file()`
does not swap immediately. It queues the change and the engine performs the
delete-old / add-new on a later idle frame -- which is exactly why it is safe to
call from `_run_transition()` in the first place. So `_run_transition()` returns,
clears the flag, and there is a window in which the old scene is still current,
or the new scene is instantiated but its `_ready()` has not run, while
`is_transitioning` already reads `false`.

Practical exposure: a `go_to()` issued in that window is accepted rather than
dropped. Two navigations then race, and which target survives depends on frame
timing -- non-deterministic, and the failure mode is "the player ends up on the
wrong screen", not a crash. I have no confirmed repro; the guard's job is to make
one impossible, and right now it does not quite.

Options:
- **A.** Hold the flag until the new scene is actually current -- clear it from
  the `SceneTree.node_added`/`tree_changed` signal, or after
  `await get_tree().process_frame` following the swap. Simple, slightly
  fudgy, probably sufficient.
- **B.** Clear it when `get_tree().current_scene` changes identity. More
  precise, still does not cover "instantiated but `_ready` pending" for the
  reload case.
- **C.** Decide the window is acceptable and document it in the class contract
  at `:23`. Defensible -- the contract comment currently says "A second request
  while one is in flight is dropped", which is the claim that is not quite true.
  If C is chosen, fix the comment; a contract that overstates its guarantee is
  the thing to avoid.

Recommendation: A, plus tightening the `:23` comment either way.

## 2. Corollary -- the `scene_load` perf measurement excludes `_ready`

CONFIRMED:

- `:90-92` -- `var sw := PerfLog.time_section("scene_load", {...})`
- `:112` -- `sw.stop()`

Same root cause: `sw.stop()` runs before the engine has swapped, so the
`scene_load` timing covers **load + instantiate only**. The new scene's `_ready()`
-- which for `main.tscn` is where `MainUI` builds the entire HUD, wires
controllers, and boots the game -- happens after the stopwatch has closed.

This does not make the number wrong, it makes it narrow. The risk is
interpretive: a fast `scene_load` reading must NOT be read as "nothing ran slowly
in `_ready`", and a slow one localises to resource load, not to game setup. Since
`PerfLog` exists to be read later by someone debugging a stall, that distinction
needs to be written down where the reader will see it.

Minimum action: a comment at `:88-92` stating what the section does and does not
cover. Better: rename the section to `scene_load_instantiate`, or open a second
section that closes in the new scene's `_ready` if a full door-to-door number is
actually wanted. Renaming may break whatever consumes the PerfLog output --
check before doing it.

## Priority

Neither part is player-visible today. (1) is a latent correctness gap in a
chokepoint whose entire justification is being the one place navigation is made
safe (`docs/LEADERBOARD_CRASH_DIAGNOSIS.md`, the v0.11.0 segfault); a guard in
that position should be airtight or should say plainly that it is not. (2) is
pure measurement hygiene, and is the #1027 pattern in miniature: an instrument
that reports a true number that reads as a claim it does not support.

Not league-blocking for Friday.

Related: #1027, #1032 (the ENTER double-fire, whose duplicate navigation is currently absorbed by this same guard), #1034 (the latent fade/pause deadlock in the same file).

issues.title: bug(config_confirmation): ENTER double-fires launch -- increment_games_played() runs twice per keyboard launch
issues.body:
Small, real, and cosmetic-plus-statistical rather than gameplay-breaking.

## Evidence (CONFIRMED)

`godot/scripts/ui/config_confirmation.gd:105-112`:
```
func _input(event: InputEvent):
	"""Handle keyboard shortcuts"""
	if event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and not event.echo:
		if event.keycode == KEY_ESCAPE:
			_on_back_pressed()
		elif event.keycode == KEY_ENTER:
			if not launch_button.disabled:
				_on_launch_pressed()
```

No `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` on either branch. Meanwhile:

- `godot/scripts/ui/config_confirmation.gd:29` -- `launch_button.grab_focus()`,
  so the Launch button holds focus on arrival.
- `godot/scenes/config_confirmation.tscn:209` --
  `[connection signal="pressed" from="Panel/VBox/ButtonRow/LaunchButton" to="." method="_on_launch_pressed"]`

INFERRED (not verified by running the game): a focused Godot `Button` activates
on `ui_accept`, which ENTER is bound to by default. Because `_input` did not mark
the event handled, the same keypress also reaches the GUI focus path and fires
the `pressed` signal. `_on_launch_pressed()` therefore runs twice per ENTER
launch.

The observable consequence is at `config_confirmation.gd:81`:
`GameConfig.increment_games_played()` runs twice. Any player who launches with
ENTER (the natural thing to do, given the button already has focus) has their
`games_played` counter inflated -- roughly 2x for keyboard players, 1x for mouse
players, which makes the statistic incoherent across the population rather than
merely wrong by a constant.

The second effect is a second navigation. `SceneTransition.go_to()` guards on
`is_transitioning` (`godot/autoload/scene_transition.gd:55-57`) and drops the
duplicate with a `push_warning`, so the double-nav is currently absorbed. That guard is doing more work than anyone intended, and it has its own defect -- see #1033.

## Not verified

I did not run the game (main is frozen, playtest in progress), so the
double-fire is INFERRED from the wiring, not observed. Cheap to confirm: launch
with ENTER twice and check whether `games_played` moved by 2 or by 4.

The ESC branch at `:108-109` has the same missing `set_input_as_handled()`, but
no competing handler is wired to Back, so it is currently harmless. Fix both
while in there.

## Fix

Add `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` inside both branches. One line each.

Wider point worth a moment's thought rather than a rule: this file is one of
several that hand-roll `_input` keyboard shortcuts alongside a focused control.
The same "shortcut handler plus focused button" shape exists elsewhere in
`godot/scripts/ui/` and each instance needs the same discipline. Not proposing a
sweep in this issue; noting that the shape is the bug, not the file.

Related: #1027 (a counter that is quietly wrong is exactly the silent-wrongness
class), and #1033.

issues.title: ui(tech-debt): 30 scene-authored placeholders read as real state -- sentinel convention, then a narrow gate
issues.body:
Follow-on from `docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md`. **Read the doc** -- it
carries the per-line tables, the rejected alternatives, and the measured false
positive rates. This issue is the actionable summary.

The two LIVE bugs from the same audit are filed as #1030; this is everything else.

## What the audit found

34 `.tscn` files under `godot/` (excluding `addons/`), 20 with `text =`
properties, 224 assignments total.

| Category  | Count | Meaning |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| DANGEROUS |    32 | reads as real runtime state |
| AMBIGUOUS |     9 | judgement calls, argued individually in the doc |
| HARMLESS  |   183 | static chrome: captions, headings, legends, keybind hints |

Of the 32 DANGEROUS, 30 are overwritten by runtime code in normal operation --
so they are **debugging traps**, live only when boot fails, which is exactly what
happened in #1023. The other 2 are the live bugs in #1030.

Worst offenders in the 30, for flavour:
- `godot/scenes/main.tscn:240` -- `58.5%`. A specific, precision-carrying,
  plausibly-mid-game doom reading. Nothing about `58.5` says "not real".
- `godot/scenes/ui/staff_perks_panel.tscn:211,218` -- `DR. ELENA VANCE`,
  `Safety Researcher | Skill 7/10`. A fully realised fake employee.
- `godot/scenes/config_confirmation.tscn:97-165` -- the entire pre-launch review
  screen is convincing fakes of the exact values the screen promises to report,
  including `weekly-2025-w45`, a week from a year the game no longer starts in.
- `godot/scenes/ui/employee_screen.tscn:86` -- `[OK] No warnings`. A positive
  ASSERTION: a dead panel claims the team is fine.
- `godot/scenes/ui/whats_new_modal.tscn:85` -- `Version 0.11.0 - Travel &
  Conferences`, a stale wrong version number.

Aggravating detail from `main.tscn`: the placeholders do not even match the
runtime FORMAT (runtime money is `GameConfig.format_money(...)` with no
`Money: ` prefix; compute/research are bare `%.1f`). So a reader cannot
distinguish "dead UI" from "old build" either.

## Proposed convention

**A node whose text is owned by runtime code MUST be authored in the scene as one
of a closed set of ASCII sentinels, never as a specimen value.**

| Sentinel | Use |
|----------|-----|
| `""` (empty) | preferred where the empty node does not collapse layout |
| `--` | a value slot (numbers, money, percentages, dates, counts) |
| `[--]` | a bracketed-chrome value slot, matching `[M]` / `[OK]` / `[!]` |
| `???` | an unknown-identity slot (names, quirks, statuses) |
| `<Label>` | a named slot where sizing needs realistic width, e.g. `<doom>` |

This codifies an existing in-repo precedent rather than importing one: the tree
already ships `???`, `---`, `[---]`, `Researcher.HIDDEN_PLACEHOLDER` in
`staff_perks_panel`, and `Avg Score: --` at
`godot/scripts/ui/leaderboard_screen.gd:606-607`. Note that last one -- that
script's own empty state already writes `--` while its scene literals at
`leaderboard_screen.tscn:195-205` assert `0`. The scene disagrees with the
script's own house style.

Crucially it degrades LOUDLY: a boot-failed HUD reading `-- | -- | Phase: --`
cannot be mistaken for turn 1.

Rejected alternatives (reasoning in the doc): empty-by-default as the *sole*
rule (Godot layout genuinely needs non-empty text to size `HBoxContainer`
Labels); `PLACEHOLDER`/`TODO` words (too long, wrecks layout worse than a real
value); a node-naming convention (renaming breaks every `$Path/To/Node` and
`@onready` in the UI layer for zero runtime benefit, and fixes nothing for the
human staring at the screen).

## Recommended sequence -- ORDER IS THE POINT

1. Fix the two live bugs (#1030).
2. **Convert the 30 remaining DANGEROUS lines to sentinels.** This is the whole
   payoff and needs no tooling.
3. **THEN** add the gate as `tools/check_scene_placeholders.py`, pre-commit on
   changed `.tscn` plus a CI full-tree pass.
4. Do NOT build the ownership-cross-reference design (Design B in the doc):
   estimated 20-40% FP rate concentrated on the interesting multi-hop cases,
   days of effort, and it rots.

Step 3 must not precede step 2. A gate added first is red on arrival against 30
pre-existing lines, gets `--no-verify`-ed once, and is then ignored forever.
That is a worse outcome than no gate.

## Honest limitation of the proposed gate -- state this up front

The gate design that survives cost/benefit (Design A: flag `text = "..."` in
`.tscn` when the value contains a digit, restricted to `Label`/`RichTextLabel`,
after stripping colour hex and `[...]` bracket spans, skipping values over ~40
chars) measures at roughly **24 true positives / 1 false positive (~4%)** on the
current tree, versus 23/15 (39%) raw.

Its problem is recall, not precision. It structurally CANNOT catch the
non-numeric DANGEROUS values -- `DR. ELENA VANCE`, `AI Safety Lab`,
`Standard (Regulatory)`, `[SAFE]`, `Phase: Not Started`, `[OK] No warnings`,
and, most importantly, `Game not started...`.

**A digit gate would NOT have caught the incident that prompted this audit.**
Anyone selling it as the fix is overselling. The audit's own estimate: it
prevents maybe 60-70% of future instances of this class and roughly 0% of the
"plausible prose status line" variant that actually cost the debugging time.
Worth doing because it is cheap, not because it closes the hole.

## Implementation constraint for whoever builds the gate

The allowlist **cannot** be inline. Godot rewrites `.tscn` on save and drops
comments, so the `# scene-nav-allow` annotation trick used by
`tools/check_scene_nav.py` does not transfer. It must be an external checked-in
file (`tools/scene_placeholder_allowlist.txt`, entries like
`path/to/scene.tscn:NodePath`). That is extra friction, and it is the reason to
keep the gate narrow enough that the allowlist stays short.

One scene is correct by construction and should be allowlisted, not converted:
`godot/scenes/welcome.tscn:155` (`v0.13.1`) is overwritten at
`welcome_screen.gd:48` AND stamped by `tools/sync_version.py`, whose `--check`
gates pre-commit and CI.

## Priority

Not league-blocking. This is a debuggability investment, and its value is
entirely realised the next time something fails to boot during a release week.
Fits #1027's thesis directly: the existing guardrails are strong at preventing
bad code and weak at detecting wrong state.

Related: #1030 (the two live bugs from the same audit), #1023, #1026, #1027, #744 (the ASCII rule the sentinels respect), #1035 (the .tscn non-ASCII side finding, which shares the external-allowlist constraint).

issues.title: ui(bug): 'Game not started...' is the permanent first line of every player's feed; 'Turn 1' label is dead
issues.body:
Two concrete bugs found by the read-only scene audit in
`docs/UI_PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT_2026-07-30.md` (34 `.tscn` files, 224 `text =`
assignments classified). Filed together because they are the same defect class,
but only (a) reaches players.

## (a) PLAYER-FACING -- `Game not started...` is the permanent first line of every feed

CONFIRMED.

`godot/scenes/ui/watch_screen.tscn:25`:
```
[node name="MessageLog" type="RichTextLabel" parent="MessageScroll"]
text = "[color=gray]Game not started...[/color]"
```

The feed writer only ever appends:
- `godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:1359` -- `message_log.text += "\n" + line`

`grep -n 'message_log.text' godot --include=*.gd` returns exactly two writes:
that `+=`, and `main_ui.gd:1384` (`message_log.text = text`) inside
`_render_feed()`, which is a full rebuild but only runs on
`_on_feed_filter_changed` / `_on_rivals_filter_changed` -- i.e. only when the
player happens to toggle a feed filter.

Consequence: in a normal run the first line of the player's message log
permanently reads `Game not started...`, above every real event line. Harm is
modest (it scrolls out of view) but it is false state shipped to players, and it
is the same string that made the dead UI in #1023 look alive. It ships Friday
unless fixed.

It also explains its own survival: anyone who flipped a feed filter while testing
watched it silently disappear.

Fix: author the scene text empty, and add an unconditional clear on the boot path
in `main_ui.gd`. The unconditional `=` is the load-bearing half -- authoring it
empty alone would leave the same hole open for the next person.

## (b) DEV-VISIBLE ONLY -- `Turn 1` is never assigned; the node is hidden instead

CONFIRMED.

`godot/scenes/main.tscn:103`:
```
[node name="TurnCountLabel" type="Label" parent="TabManager/MainUI/TopBar"]
text = "Turn 1"
```

`godot/scripts/ui/main_ui.gd:1060` does `turn_count_label.visible = false` (the
date badge at `TurnLabel` supersedes it; the merge is explained in the comment at
`main_ui.gd:1057`). The `.text` is written nowhere in the tree.

So: when the UI is alive the label is hidden; when boot fails the label is
visible reading `Turn 1`. No live-player impact -- but it is the worst-behaved
variant of the class, because the placeholder is displayed **only** in the
failure case. It contributed directly to #1023 reading as a gameplay bug rather
than a boot failure.

Fix: delete the `text` property (or the node -- it is dead UI). Not a sentinel
change; there is nothing to sentinel.

## The generalisable rule this exposes

**`+=` does not establish runtime ownership of a node's text.** Only an
unconditional `=` on a boot path does. Any node written exclusively via `+=` must
be authored empty in the scene and cleared explicitly at boot.

This rule matters beyond these two nodes: it is the one invariant that an
automated checker could use to distinguish "runtime owns this label" from
"runtime decorates this label", and it is why the audit's ownership-analysis
design (Design B) was the only proposed gate that would have flagged (a) at all.

## Priority

(a) is small but is live player-facing wrongness in the Friday build. (b) is
cosmetic-until-something-breaks and can ride any later cleanup.

Related: #1023 (the boot failure these dressed up), #1027 (silent wrongness as
the dominant failure mode), and #1031 (the remaining 30 DANGEROUS placeholders + the proposed sentinel convention).
